## What's new in this version

A chore release whose only purpose is to prove, em uma release real, que the
release image era declared in `.github/release.config.json` travels with the
tag.

- The release art is now declared as an **era** instead of being resolved by
  filename. `changes: [{ "from": "v1.1.0", "file": "release-v1.1.webp" }]` means
  the intent is reviewable in the diff, instead of the filename quietly meaning
  "the line 1.1" while the bytes mean "since whenever somebody last replaced
  the file".
- The image is now **survives a re-execution**. The art is the only release asset
  that comes from the checkout rather than from the build, so a re-run from
  `main` used to replace the published image with whatever `main` had, silently
  and under the same asset name. A per-line file that is not rewritten in place
  removes that class of surprise.
- Release Core pinned to `@v1.3.0`, which is where the era support and the
  content-based art gate live.
- The dependency gate that had this repository unable to push at all
  (`security:audit`, three high-severity transitives) is fixed, so the five
  Dependabot pull requests that were stuck are reviewable again.

No user-facing change. The site builds the same as it did in v1.1.0, and the
cover art is the same file that v1.1.0 already served - now declared rather than
assumed.
